newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent charts brake rally, supports say up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent charts brake rally, supports say up.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20 BRENT 20.13 * 20.00 * 20.34 * 66 * 19.27 * 18.77
* For Brent crude the target $20.50 remains intact with good support in a band between $19.25 and $19.50 which represents a period of congestion on the July chart between May 12-15.
* On candlestick charts a long legged Doji on Tuesday followed up by a Hanging Man on Wednesday, are signs that the rally may be ending.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures may continue to track sideways, but while chart formations flag an end to the recent rally, some analysts saw solid supports offering a longer term chance to move still higher.

The prompt July Brent contract closed up 12 cents at $20.12 a barrel, just four cents off the day's high, but failed to break above flag resistance at $20.34, a close above which could have opened up a run to $21.40 a barrel, brokers said.
The markets recent uptrend from last Friday now appears to have stalled and may be at an end.

The appearance of a long legged Doji on Tuesday, a market at top sign according to Japanese candlestick charting techniques, was followed up by a Hanging Man on Wednesday, a sign that a rally may be ending.

Analysts said that this sentiment was backed up by low historic volatility levels of around 33.4 and 27.6 percent measured over 10 and 20-day periods respectively, neutral momentum indicators and recently low trading volumes.
IPE brokers said trading volume on Brent was low on Wednesday and "extremely thin" in the pre-NYMEX trade, but added that with the long weekend coming up trade could be quite "volatile".
However, brokers said they expected July Brent to be supported at $20.00, a 50-percent retracement of last Friday's rally.

Taking a more bullish stance, Nicholas Wilson, analyst at MeesPierson said the target $20.50 remains intact though the market has pulled back a little. He saw good support in a band between $19.25 and $19.50 which represents a period of congestion on the July chart between May 12-15.
"Ultimately the next target is $20.20 with a further upside target at $21.35 and then taking out contract highs of $21.90," Wilson said.

He saw a similar pattern of trade for gas oil with the markets recent pull back having been very modest and its failure to fill a recent gap up and pull away from the highs and indication the market still has plenty of room to improve.
IPE gas oil futures ended slightly lower in thin trade. The June contract settled $1.50 down at $176.25 a tonne.

The $173 to $176.50 gap-up from last Friday to Monday remained supportively intact. But after two days of consolidation a shooting star formation, though not perfect, on Wednesday's front month continuation chart, indicated that bulls are finding it difficult to gain control.
NYMEX crude oil futures and unleaded gasoline rallied at the close of trading to settle broadly higher on reports that Turkish forces had staged another incursion across the border of Iraq.
Heating oil, took a back seat to the rest of the action, but ended mostly firmer, with only the June contract settling lower.
July crude rose 27 cents, settling at $21.86 a barrel after trading in a $21.95-$21.46 range.
News of the Mideast hostility caused a fresh wave of short covering and brought in a few new longs in crude oil.
Unleaded gasoline matched the crude rally, settling with broad gains after what was a choppy session for the whole complex.

Brokers said they expected the market to remain supported by news of Turkish incursions into northern Iraq, which is unnerving neighbours. Turkey's state-run news agency Anatolian said Syria, Iraq and Iran were building up forces on the borders of the Kurdish safe-haven in northern Iraq.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
